## Background 

There are many *graphics systems* in R for making plots and figures. These include **"base R graphics"** like the `plot()` and add-on packages like **ggplot2**. 

Let's compare how we make a simple graph with these two systems:

We can use the in-built `cars` data set:

```{r}
head(cars)
```
A base R plot:
```{r}
plot(cars)
```

Now for **ggplot2**:
Before I can use ggplot2, I need to install it on my computes. To do this, we can use the function `install.packages('ggplot2')`. 

> **NEVER** run an `install.packages("")` in our Quarto doc (run it in R console), as it would re-install the package everytime a document is rendered

Once installed, the package still needs to be loaded into our R session. We do this with our `library()` call. 

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(cars)
```

Every ggplot needs at least 3 inputs:

- The **data** (a `data.frame()` of the data we want to plot)
- The **aesthetics** (how the data maps to the plot)
- The **geometry** layer (how you want the plot drawn, points, lines, etc.)

```{r}
ggplot(data=cars) +
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) +
  geom_point()
```

## Let's add some features (more layers)

Let's add a trend line that shows the relationship between `speed` and `distance`:
```{r}
ggplot(data=cars) +
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method=lm, se=F) +
  theme_gray() +
  labs(x='Speed in mph', 
       y='Stopping Distance in ft',
       title='Stopping distance of some old cars')
```

## Gene Expression Plot

First we will read some expression data for the effects of a GLP-1 drug.

```{r}
url <- 'https://bioboot.github.io/bimm143_S20/class-material/up_down_expression.txt'
genes <- read.delim(url)
head(genes)
```

> Q. Use the `nrow()` function to find out how many genes are in this dataset. What is your answer?

```{r}
nrow(genes)
```

> Q. Use the `colnames()` function and the `ncol()` function on the genes data frame to find out what the column names are (we will need these later) and how many columns there are. How many columns did you find?

```{r}
colnames(genes)
ncol(genes)
```

> Q. Use the table() function on the State column of this data.frame to find out how many ‘up’ regulated genes there are. What is your answer? 

```{r}
table(genes$State)
```
>Q. Using your values above and 2 significant figures. What fraction of total genes is up-regulated in this dataset?

```{r}
up_reg <- sum(genes$State=='up')
total <- nrow(genes)

round(up_reg/total, 2)

```

```{r}
ggplot(data=genes) +
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2, col=State) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c('blue','grey','red')) +
  labs(y='Drug Treatment', 
  x='Control (no drug)', 
  title='GLP-1 Inhibitor Effects on Gene Expression') +
  theme_bw()
  
```

## Going Further

Here we read the famous `gapmider` dataset:

```{r}
# File location online
url2 <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/master/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv"

gapminder <- read.delim(url2)
head(gapminder)
```

> Q. How many entries are in this data set?

```{r}
nrow(gapminder)
```

> Q. How many different countries are in this data set?

```{r}
length(table(gapminder$country))

#or
length(unique(gapminder$country))
```

Let's make our first plot:

**1. GDP/capita (`gdpPercap`) vs Life Expectancy (`lifeExp`):**

```{r}
ggplot(data=gapminder) +
  aes(x=gdpPercap, y=lifeExp, col=continent) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.3) + #transparency from 0-1
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x='GDP/Capita', 
       y='Life Expectancy', 
       title='Comparing GDP/Capita and Life Expectancy')
```

One useful layer we can add to explore big data is called "faceting"

```{r}
ggplot(data=gapminder) +
  aes(x=gdpPercap, y=lifeExp, col=continent) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.5) + #transparency from 0-1
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x='GDP/Capita', 
       y='Life Expectancy', 
       title='Comparing GDP/Capita and Life Expectancy') +
  facet_wrap(~continent) #makes separate panels for each continent 
```


### Limit the data set to 1977 and 2007

Need to first install dplyr (`install.packages('dplyr'))`) that allows us to filter the dataset down to a subset that only includes the years we want.
```{r}
library(dplyr)

filter(gapminder, year==2007, country=='India')
filter(gapminder, year==1977, country=='India')

```


> Q. Make a histogram of the `lifeExp` and color it by continent

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp, fill=continent) +
  geom_histogram()
```

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp, fill=continent) +
  geom_boxplot()
```
